title: GC/MS Method for the Detection of Terbufos, Diazinon and Parathion in Blood
author: Christina Wilson-Frank
materials: Inject 1 µL of the reconstituted sample extract into a GC/MS that is equipped with a triple quadrupole mass spectrometer under conditions found in Table 1. Initial results have shown that the use of an ion-trap mass spectrometer has significantly higher instrument and method LODs when compared to using triple quadrupole MS.Table 1: Instrument Parameters for GC/MS for the Detection of Terbufos, Diazinon, and Parathion in Blood Samples GC Parameters Initial Oven Temp and Hold 40 C for 0.5 min Final Oven Temp and Hold 300 C for 1.0 min Injector Temp 275 C (splitless) Carrier Gas Flow 1.4 ml/min Injection Volume 1 µL Column ThermoFisher TR-5 Column Size 30 m X 0.25 mm Column Film Size 0.25 µL Rinse for Autosampler Toluene MS Parameters Transfer Line Temp 325 C Ion Source Temp 310 C Ionization Mode EI Scan Range 50-650 m/z Quadrupole Temp MS Type Triple Quadrupole

Possible solutions to help reduce the fatty acid concentrations during the preparation of the sample: Switch from sodium sulfate to magnesium sulfate as previous research has shown sodium sulfate is not as effective drying agent for acetonitrile solutions. Change the extraction/elution solvents during the process.Solutions in published literature include using acetone, acetone:toluene (65:35), and acetone:cyclohexane (various compositions) with the current SPE cartridges containing PSA.

steps.title: Prepare solvent mixture
steps.instruction: Measure 600 mL acetonitrile into a 1 L graduated cylinder, add 200 mL toluene, mix, then transfer to a properly labeled 1 L glass storage bottle and store at room temperature.

steps.title: Label storage bottle
steps.instruction: Write on the bottle: contents, expiration date (earliest of the two reagents), laboratory notebook reference, analyst initials, and hazard communication designations.

steps.title: Record reagent information
steps.instruction: In the laboratory notebook, record manufacturer, part number, lot number, and expiration date for all standards and reagents used.

steps.title: Prepare 20 ppm mixed standard
steps.instruction: Pipette 1.50 mL of the acetonitrile:toluene (3:1) solvent into a 5 mL glass vial, add 0.75 mL each of 100 ppm terbufos, 100 ppm diazinon, and 100 ppm parathion, then label the vial with contents, expiration date (earliest of the reagents), notebook reference, analyst initials, and hazard designations.

steps.title: Prepare 1 ppm mixed standard
steps.instruction: Aliquot 2.00 mL of the acetonitrile:toluene (3:1) solvent into a new 5 mL glass vial, add 106 µL of the 20 ppm mixed standard prepared above, and label the vial with the same information as above.

steps.title: Prepare negative control blood
steps.instruction: Transfer 2 mL pesticide‑free blood into a properly labeled 15 mL polypropylene tube; this tube will be processed in the sample‑prep steps.

steps.title: Prepare positive control blood
steps.instruction: Transfer 2 mL pesticide‑free blood into a properly labeled tube, add 106 µL of the 20 ppm mixed standard to achieve a 1 ppm spike, then proceed to the sample‑prep steps.

steps.title: Aliquot blood sample
steps.instruction: Aliquot 2 mL of each test blood sample into a properly labeled 15 mL polypropylene tube and record sample ID, volume, and any other pertinent information in the notebook.

steps.title: Add acetonitrile and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 4 mL acetonitrile to each tube, vortex for approximately 00:01:00 (1 minute).

steps.title: First centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at approximately 4,000 RPM (~1,500 RCF) for 00:10:00 (10 minutes).

steps.title: Transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Aliquot the clear supernatant into a properly labeled 15 mL polypropylene tube.

steps.title: Add second acetonitrile aliquot and vortex
steps.instruction: Add an additional 4 mL acetonitrile to the remaining pellet, vortex for approximately 00:01:00 (1 minute).

steps.title: Second centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge again at approximately 4,000 RPM (~1,500 RCF) for 00:10:00 (10 minutes).

steps.title: Combine supernatants
steps.instruction: Aliquot the second supernatant and combine it with the supernatant collected in step 5.

steps.title: Add sodium sulfate and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 1 g anhydrous Na₂SO₄ to the combined supernatants, vortex for approximately 00:01:00 (1 minute) to dry the extract, then allow the Na₂SO₄ to settle.

steps.title: Transfer dried extract
steps.instruction: Using a disposable glass pipet, transfer all of the dried acetonitrile extract to a 15 mL polypropylene tube (extract is stable for 24 hours under refrigeration).

steps.title: Condition SPE cartridge
steps.instruction: Condition a multi‑layer Supelclean ENVI‑Carb‑II/PSA SPE cartridge (20 mL or 6 mL capacity) with 5 mL acetonitrile:toluene (3:1); collect the eluate as waste in a properly labeled waste beaker.

steps.title: Load extract onto SPE
steps.instruction: Load the acetonitrile extract from step 14 onto the conditioned SPE cartridge; collect the flow‑through as waste in the same waste beaker.

steps.title: Elute pesticides from SPE
steps.instruction: Elute the retained pesticides with 15 mL acetonitrile:toluene (3:1) into a properly labeled 50 mL glass test tube.

steps.title: Evaporate eluate to dryness
steps.instruction: Place the test tube in a nitrogen evaporator heating block set to approximately 40 °C and evaporate the eluate to dryness under low nitrogen flow (dry residue stable for 24 hours under refrigeration).

steps.title: Reconstitute residue and filter
steps.instruction: Reconstitute the dried residue with 0.5 mL acetonitrile:toluene (3:1), vortex well to dissolve completely, then transfer to spin‑X microcentrifuge tubes equipped with nylon filters.

steps.title: Transfer to autosampler vial
steps.instruction: Vortex the filtered tubes for 00:00:30 (30 seconds), then transfer the filtrate to a properly labeled GC/MS autosampler vial containing a vial insert (solution stable for 24 hours under refrigeration).

steps.title: Set GC/MS instrument method
steps.instruction: Use the GC/MS method titled “Pesticide Screen Tox.103 20 min”; inject 1 µL of the reconstituted sample; the instrument is a Trace 1310 GC with TSQ 8000 MS and TriPlus RSH autosampler, operating under the conditions listed in Table 1 of the method.

steps.title: Apply acceptance criteria for detection
steps.instruction: Confirm that for each pesticide the retention time is within 3 % of the positive‑control or 1 ppm standard, the signal‑to‑noise ratio exceeds 3 RMS, all listed ions are present (Terbufos 231/103/153 m/z, Diazinon 137/179/152/199 m/z, Parathion 109/139/291 m/z), secondary‑ion intensities are within 30 % of the major ion, and the fatty‑acid‑to‑terbufos S/N ratio does not exceed the alert threshold defined by Equation 1.
